title: Nursery 1 Numeracy
subject: Numeracy
philosophy: Numeracy in Nursery 1 is learnt by handling, counting, comparing and talking about real things: stones, seeds, bottle tops, fruit, blocks and the children themselves. Every idea starts with objects, moves to pictures and songs, and only then to written numerals. ELA’s Nursery 1 Numeracy keeps lessons short, active and playful, and builds a firm, confident feel for numbers to 10 before children meet formal sums.
rationale: Children who arrive in Nursery 1 can usually count to about five. This programme takes them to counting 10 objects accurately, recognising and forming numerals 1 to 10, comparing sizes, lengths, weights and amounts, naming common shapes, making patterns and solving small real-life problems by joining and taking away. It uses everyday Nigerian contexts such as the market, naira coins, fruit, school bags and games so that mathematics makes sense to children.
aims: To count objects to 10 accurately and say the number names in order.
To recognise and begin to write the numerals 1 to 10.
To compare and order objects by size, length, weight and capacity using everyday words.
To sort, match, make patterns and name common shapes.
To understand more, fewer, one more and one less, and to join and take away small groups.
To talk about time, position, money and simple data in daily life.
learningOutcomes: Counts to 10 and counts up to 10 objects, touching each once.
Recognises numerals 1 to 10 and matches them to quantities.
Sorts and matches objects by one or two features such as colour and size.
Compares size, length, weight and capacity with words such as bigger, longer, heavier and fuller.
Names circles, squares, triangles, rectangles and ovals and finds them around the class.
Says which group has more or fewer and finds one more and one less.
Joins two small groups and takes away from a group with objects, up to 5.
Continues and makes simple repeating patterns.
Uses everyday words for time, position and money.
developmentalExpectations: Children learn to count by moving objects as they say each number, not just by saying the number names.
Counting a group of more than five accurately is a major milestone and needs plenty of practice.
Children grasp "how many in all" after they can count each object once; do not rush.
Writing numerals is hard for small hands; use sand, air tracing, large pencils and clay before paper.
Concentration is short; each lesson has several short activities and plenty of movement.

strands.title: Number and counting
strands.description: Counting, numerals, more and fewer to 10 and beyond.

priorKnowledge: Children are expected to count to about five with objects, recognise a few shapes and use words such as big and small. Observe in the first two weeks how far each child counts and record it as the baseline.
yearProgression: Term 1 builds counting and numerals to 10, sorting and matching, size and length comparisons, and the shapes circle, square and triangle.
Term 2 builds more and fewer, one more and one less, counting beyond 10, numeral order, making 5, joining and taking away, rectangles and ovals, and patterns.
Term 3 builds weight and capacity, time and ordinal numbers, tallying, picture graphs, money, position, and number stories.
assessmentPrinciples: Assessment is by watching, listening and recording what children do and say with real objects. There are no written tests.
Levels Emerging, Developing, Secure and Exceeding follow the lesson success criteria (see ASSESSMENT_FRAMEWORK.md).
Check counting by asking a child to count out a number of objects, not only to recite numbers.
Share with parents in plain language, always with a strength, a next step and a home idea.
inclusion: Every lesson has a support and an extension version.
Use large, tactile objects for children who need them and let children count at their own pace.
Use home-language number names alongside English and celebrate them.
Offer movement, song and games for children who find sitting hard.
crossCurricular: Literacy: number rhymes, stories and vocabulary.
Science: sorting, measuring and comparing natural materials.
Social Habits: turn-taking, sharing equally and working in pairs.
EYFS mapping: Mathematics, with Communication and Language and Physical Development (see STANDARDS_ALIGNMENT.md).
parentConnection: Every lesson ends with a short home idea using safe household objects.
Parents are invited to count with their child in daily life: steps, stairs, fruit and coins.
Families are invited to share number words in their home language.
